output.sql:
SELECT ROUND(SUM(o.net_revenue) / COUNT(DISTINCT o.customer_id), 2) AS avg_revenue_per_customer_2025
FROM marts.fct_orders o
WHERE o.is_revenue
  AND o.order_date >= DATE '2025-01-01'
  AND o.order_date < DATE '2026-01-01';
output.explanation: The query uses fct_orders filtered to is_revenue = true (the warehouse's definition of revenue orders) with order_date in 2025. It sums net_revenue and divides by the number of distinct customers with at least one revenue order in 2025. That equals the average of per-customer 2025 revenue, restricted to customers who bought something in 2025. I interpreted "bought something" as having a revenue-counting order; if non-revenue orders (e.g., cancelled) should also count as purchases, the customer count would change.
